title: The connected components of the affine line over a base
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $B$ be a nonempty $k$-scheme whose structure morphism
$B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated and of finite type
[def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $\mathbf A^1_B=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_B(\mathcal O_B[t])$ be the affine line of [def-sbc-affine-space], let
$s_0:B\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_B$ be the zero section, the closed
immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] defined by $t=0$, and let
$\mathbf G_{m,B}=\mathbf A^1_B\setminus s_0(B)$ be the complement of
the zero section. Let $1:B\to\mathbf A^1_B$ be the unit section,
the section defined by $t=1$ of the projection, which factors through
$\mathbf G_{m,B}$.

1. The connected components of $\mathbf A^1_B$, and those of
$\mathbf G_{m,B}$, are exactly the inverse images of the
connected components of $B$.
1. Every connected component of $\mathbf A^1_B$ meets
$\mathbf G_{m,B}$, and meets the image of the unit section
$1$.
1. Every connected component of $\mathbf G_{m,B}$ meets the image
of the unit section $1$.

Here a connected component means a maximal nonempty connected subset of the underlying topological space, with connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme].

proof.text: Put p = the affine-line projection of [def-sbc-affine-space], and q = j followed by p. Mathlib AffineSpace.isOpenMap_over proves p open directly (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/AffineSpace.lean:390-404), so composition with the open embedding j makes q open. Both maps are continuous. The supplied unit lift satisfies i₁ followed by q = identity, using hi₁ and AffineSpace.oneSection_comp_over; hence q is surjective. Surjectivity of p is the existing affine-space instance.

Every p-fibre is irreducible, hence connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. In Lean this is the one-line specialization p.isIrreducible_preimage hpopen isIrreducible_singleton (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Geometrically/Irreducible.lean:74-85), with the existing GeometricallyIrreducible affine-space projection instance (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/AffineSpace.lean:407-412). That instance uses the affine-base polynomial spectrum formula of [def-sbc-affine-space], whose polynomial ring over a field is a domain; it already proves the original plan’s fibre calculation and generic-point argument.

The q-fibre over y is j⁻¹(p⁻¹({y})). Its preirreducibility follows from that of the p-fibre by IsPreirreducible.preimage applied to the open embedding j (Mathlib/Topology/Irreducible.lean:432-435). It is nonempty because i₁(y) projects to y, so it is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. This is the original open-subspace argument, with no localization algebra.

For f = p or q, the open continuous surjection is a quotient map by IsOpenMap.isQuotientMap. Apply Topology.IsCoinducing.preimage_connectedComponent (Mathlib/Topology/Connected/Clopen.lean:487-493) with the connected fibres just proved. This packages [lem-weil-pbc-connected-fibres-quotient-preimage-connected] applied to the closed connected component, together with continuity and maximality, and gives connectedComponent(x) = f⁻¹(connectedComponent(f(x))).

For x in the affine line, set y = p(x). The point j(i₁(y)) belongs to the component of x by the p-component formula and q(i₁(y)) = y; it also lies in range(j). The point oneSection(y) likewise belongs to that component and to the unit-section range because p(oneSection(y)) = y. For x in G take i₁(q(x)); the q-component formula and the section identity show that it belongs to the component of x and to range(i₁). These are the three requested nonempty intersections.

lean.statement: theorem affineLine_connectedComponents (P : WeilConjectures.PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) {B : Scheme.{u}} (b : B ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k)) [Nonempty B] [IsSeparated b] [LocallyOfFiniteType b] [QuasiCompact b] {G : Scheme.{u}} (j : G ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) B) [IsOpenImmersion j] (hj : Set.range j.base = (Set.range (AffineSpace.zeroSection (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) B).base)ᶜ) (i₁ : B ⟶ G) (hi₁ : i₁ ≫ j = AffineSpace.oneSection (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) B) : (∀ x : AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) B, connectedComponent x = (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) B ↘ B).base ⁻¹' connectedComponent ((AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) B ↘ B).base x)) ∧ (∀ x : G, connectedComponent x = (j ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) B ↘ B)).base ⁻¹' connectedComponent ((j ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) B ↘ B)).base x)) ∧ (∀ x : AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) B, (connectedComponent x ∩ Set.range j.base).Nonempty) ∧ (∀ x : AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) B, (connectedComponent x ∩ Set.range (AffineSpace.oneSection (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) B).base).Nonempty) ∧ (∀ x : G, (connectedComponent x ∩ Set.range i₁.base).Nonempty)
